title: Token Sampling Uncertainty Does Not Explain Homogeneity Bias in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting models to generate stories about Black and White individuals and measuring the homogeneity of the generated text using cosine similarity of sentence embeddings, as well as analyzing token-level sampling uncertainty metrics (entropy and probability of differentiation).

Prompting models to generate stories about men and women and measuring output homogeneity via cosine similarity of sentence embeddings, alongside an analysis of token-level sampling uncertainty (entropy and probability of differentiation).

Evaluating the interaction between race and gender by prompting models for stories about four intersectional groups (Black men, Black women, White men, White women) and using regression models to analyze differences in sentence embedding similarity and sampling uncertainty.
